text:
Sam Reinhart reached 700 career points with a highlight goal in St. Louis on Nov. 14, per Sports Illustrated, another marker for a two-time Stanley Cup winner. He has 12 goals and 23 points in 24 games, and his chance creation is well up on last season: 1.71 expected goals per 60, up from 1.28 last season. Expected goals measure the quality of the chances a player gets, and few forwards get better ones.

He has actually scored a little less than those chances deserve (12 goals on 13.7 expected), so his own finishing isn't the worry. His team's is. Florida has scored 7.2 more goals than expected with him on the ice, yet at five on five the Panthers take only 46% of the expected goals when he plays, 7 points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey noted last season most of his value came on the penalty kill, against competition in the 97th percentile, which suggests hard minutes. Our numbers project 29 to 43 goals. The sign to watch is whether his five-on-five share climbs back to normal.
headline: Reinhart hits 700 with chances to spare
